title: Shared toolchain image, per-repo env pin
rationale: Reuse is key (user directive): not every repo needs its own toolchain build; the seeds image already carries rust nightly, mise tools, seeds and ml. Env creation goes through the server API POST /api/v1/environments (fabro env CLI has no create).

description:
Shell trap confirmed twice in one session (fabro sprint 19-21): passing a CLI argument that contains BACKTICKS through bash() makes bash run it as command substitution before the tool ever sees it — `seeds create --title "... the `duplicates` check ..."` silently created a seed whose title read 'the  check', and `ml record --name "the `x` seam"` would do the same. Second instance of the same family as the crashed-pipe lesson: the tool call SUCCEEDS while its argument is mangled, so only reading the stored value back reveals it.

RULE: never inline text with backticks, $(), or quotes directly in a bash() command line. Write the argument to a file first (python open().write) and pass it as $(cat /tmp/file) — and read the stored value back (seed show / record query) before trusting it.
resolution: write every argument to a file first, always pass it as $(cat /tmp/file) (never inline backticks, quotes or $()), and read the stored value back before trusting the call

title: jsval owns the UTF-16 truncate
rationale: The reference ONE truncate (utils/format-helpers.ts) counts and slices UTF-16 CODE UNITS: 31 emoji (62 units) cut at 60 keeps 30+..., 51 emoji cut at 100 keeps 50+..., a cut splitting a surrogate pair renders U+FFFD (Node UTF-8 stdout conversion of a lone surrogate). Rust chars() and bytes() BOTH diverge on non-ASCII - jsval::js_truncate (encode_utf16 + from_utf16_lossy) is the law; sentence-end = first [.!?] + the ECMAScript whitespace set (NBSP counts, NEL does not - differs from Rust White_Space both ways), applied only inside the window, index 0 never wins.

name: nu-0116-compat-checked-pin-blocked-on-seeds-image
description: mulch's 27 nu scripts are nushell 0.116.1-compatible (2026-10-17, nushell-pro 0.116 migration reference): no completers/tui/yaml --compact-list-indent/simple-parse-brace usages; lint-nu green and rotate-sprint-notes dry-run byte-identical under 0.116.1. The .mise.toml pin stays 0.115.0 ANYWAY: it mirrors the SHARED seeds toolchain image (Dockerfile.toolchain pins aqua:nushell/nushell@0.115.0) and run sandboxes resolve nu through /workspace/.mise.toml — a local-only bump would force runtime installs in runs. Switch order: seeds image bumps first, then this repo's mirror.

name: seeds-config-vcs-manager-enum
description: seeds .seeds/config.yaml vcs_manager accepts git|gitbutler (absent = git; 'git' is skipped on serialize), but 'seeds config set vcs_manager git' is REJECTED by the config schema (additionalProperties=vcs_manager — the key is not in the emitted JSON schema). To switch modes: 'seeds config unset vcs_manager' (lands on the git default and validates) or hand-edit the YAML. The gitbutler value makes seeds sync REPORT-ONLY instead of git add + git commit (crates/seeds dedupe_sync). Learned 2026-10-17 during the GitButler teardown (mulch-6817).

scripts/qualitygate.nu routes a changed root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock to `cargo check --workspace` (to stay under the tester timeout) instead of the touched-crates clippy+test arm. A sprint whose FIRST commit adds a dependency (sprint 42: libc for the hook engine) therefore reports 'workspace compiles' and GATE GREEN while the new source carries clippy -D warnings findings — they surfaced only when a later manifest-free commit ran the normal arm. Symptom to watch: a gate run that prints '== cargo check --workspace -- root manifest changed ==' without a clippy line.
resolution: Filed as mulch-d9b2 (gate should clippy the crates whose sources changed, or print an explicit 'clippy unverified' line). Workaround until then: when the gate takes the root-manifest branch, run `cargo +nightly-2026-09-22 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` by hand before closing the sprint.

description: Both sprint-54 parallel children flagged it independently: the machine now hosts TWO ml installs (0.10.7 project-pinned via .mise.toml, 0.11.0 machine-level); mise puts 0.11.0 first on PATH for processes spawned OUTSIDE the repo, while the devshell and in-repo cargo runs resolve the project pin 0.10.7. 0.11.0 ADDS a top-level quality config knob and changes the onboard snippet - the exact-byte differential pins are correct for 0.10.7 and FAIL against 0.11.0. Symptom of the wrong reference: schema-bytes or onboard-snippet batteries failing only in scratch copies.
resolution: In-repo battery runs are safe (the .mise.toml project pin wins when cwd is inside the repo - verified: the 23144-byte schema battery is green in-repo, red in /tmp copies). For out-of-repo verification, pin the PATH explicitly: env PATH="$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/npm-os-eco-mulch-cli/0.10.7/node_modules/.bin:...bun...:$HOME/.cargo/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" with real cargo via rustup (the mise cargo shim rewrites PATH; bun must be on PATH for ml to spawn). Durable fix when the cutover (mulch-96ed) renames the reference to ml-ref: pin at install time and drop the ambiguity.
